lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet customers and coworkers and pronounce key shop words like carro, llanta and llave.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Greet a customer at the counter, say your name and that you are the mechanic, and welcome them to the shop.

items.note: rr is a strong trill: CA-rro. A single r between vowels is a quick tap.
ll sounds like English y: YAN-ta.
Also means key. ll sounds like y: YA-ve.
Short, pure vowels: GA-to. Also means cat.
ch sounds like English ch in church.
j sounds like a strong English h: ca-HUE-la. Common Mexican word.
Say every vowel: a-SEI-te.
The written accent marks the stress: ba-te-RÍ-a.
Stress falls on the last syllable: ta-YER.
A woman is la mecánica.

items.native: Good morning, my name is Carlos.
Nice to meet you, I'm the mechanic.
items.note: A woman says: soy la mecánica.
Formal usted: use it with customers.
To a woman: bienvenida.

passage.target: Carlos trabaja en el taller de la calle Juárez.
passage.native: Carlos works at the shop on Juárez Street.

passage.target: El señor Rojas llega al mostrador con su carro.
passage.native: Mr. Rojas arrives at the counter with his car.

passage.target: Carlos: Buenos días, me llamo Carlos.
passage.native: Carlos: Good morning, my name is Carlos.

passage.target: Carlos: Mucho gusto, soy el mecánico.
passage.native: Carlos: Nice to meet you, I'm the mechanic.

passage.target: Carlos: Bienvenido al taller.
passage.native: Carlos: Welcome to the shop.

passage.target: Señor Rojas: La llanta está baja y la batería está débil.
passage.native: Mr. Rojas: The tire is low and the battery is weak.

passage.target: Carlos pone el gato bajo el chasis del carro.
passage.native: Carlos puts the jack under the car's chassis.

passage.target: Carlos quita la llanta con la llave.
passage.native: Carlos takes off the tire with the wrench.

passage.target: Señor Rojas: El aceite está en la cajuela.
passage.native: Mr. Rojas: The oil is in the trunk.

example.target: Mucho gusto, soy el mecánico.
example.native: Nice to meet you, I'm the mechanic.

verbs.note: Irregular verb. Use ser to say who you are and what your job is.

example.target: El aceite está en la cajuela.
example.native: The oil is in the trunk.

verbs.note: Use estar for where something is and how it is (la llanta está baja). The forms estás, está and están carry a written accent.

verbs.native: to be called, to be named

example.target: Buenos días, me llamo Carlos.
example.native: Good morning, my name is Carlos.

verbs.note: Reflexive verb. The ll sounds like the y in yes.

example.target: Carlos trabaja en el taller.
example.native: Carlos works at the shop.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The j sounds like a strong English h.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Say times, counts and shop quantities like quarts, PSI and socket sizes.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Tell a coworker the appointment time, how many quarts the manual lists, and the PSI on the door sticker.

items.note: Common US shop word; read it from the odometer.
In the US, oil is sold by the quart.
For tire pressure, libras means PSI.
Say the system: de 10 milímetros or de media pulgada.

items.target: Según el manual, lleva 5 cuartos de aceite.
items.native: According to the manual, it takes 5 quarts of oil.
items.note: Oil capacity varies by vehicle; always check the manual.

items.target: La etiqueta de la puerta dice 35 libras.
items.note: Tire pressure varies by vehicle; read the door label.

items.native: The tire is missing 2 lug nuts.
I'll be back in half an hour.

passage.target: Ana mira la hora en el Taller García: son las 8:00.
passage.native: Ana checks the time at García Shop: it is 8:00.

passage.target: Luis: La cita es a las 8:30.
passage.native: Luis: The appointment is at 8:30.

passage.target: El millaje del carro de la señora Ruiz es de 98,500 millas.
passage.native: The mileage on Mrs. Ruiz's car is 98,500 miles.

passage.target: Ana: Según el manual, lleva 5 cuartos de aceite.
passage.native: Ana: According to the manual, it takes 5 quarts of oil.

passage.target: Luis quita el tornillo de drenaje del cárter para sacar el aceite viejo.
passage.native: Luis removes the drain bolt from the oil pan to drain the old oil.

passage.target: Luis: La etiqueta de la puerta dice 35 libras.
passage.native: Luis: The door sticker says 35 PSI.

passage.target: Ana: Faltan 2 tuercas en la llanta.
passage.native: Ana: The tire is missing 2 lug nuts.

passage.target: Ana busca un dado de 3/4 de pulgada para las tuercas de la llanta.
passage.native: Ana looks for a 3/4-inch socket for the tire's lug nuts.

passage.target: Luis: Regreso en media hora con un galón de anticongelante.
passage.native: Luis: I'll be back in half an hour with a gallon of antifreeze.

example.target: La cita es a las 8:30.
example.native: The appointment is at 8:30.

verbs.note: Irregular. Use ser to tell time: es la una, son las 8:00.

example.target: Según el manual, lleva 5 cuartos de aceite.
example.native: According to the manual, it takes 5 quarts of oil.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In the shop, lleva tells how much fluid a vehicle takes.

example.target: La etiqueta de la puerta dice 35 libras.
example.native: The door sticker says 35 PSI.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (digo). Stem change e to i (dices, dice), except nosotros.

example.target: Regreso en media hora.
example.native: I'll be back in half an hour.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The present tense often talks about the near future.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what a car or part is and describe its condition or location with ser and estar.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Describe a car on the lift to a coworker: say what it is and whether the oil is low or a tire is worn.

items.note: Some shops also say la rampa.
Mexican usage; other regions say el capó.
estar: a condition that can change.
The adjective matches: la llanta gastada, el tornillo gastado.

items.target: El carro está en el elevador.
items.native: The car is on the lift.
items.note: estar for location.
ser: what something is. Troca is common US and Mexican usage.

passage.target: Luis y Ana son mecánicos en el taller Rivera.
passage.native: Luis and Ana are mechanics at the Rivera shop.

passage.target: Una troca está en el elevador y Luis la revisa.
passage.native: A truck is on the lift, and Luis checks it.

passage.target: Luis: Es una troca Ford.
passage.native: Luis: It's a Ford truck.

passage.target: Luis: El aceite está bajo y el filtro está sucio.
passage.native: Luis: The oil is low and the filter is dirty.

passage.target: Luis: La llanta está gastada y un tornillo está flojo.
passage.native: Luis: The tire is worn and a bolt is loose.

passage.target: Ana: ¿El líquido de frenos está vacío?
passage.native: Ana: Is the brake fluid empty?

passage.target: Luis: No, el depósito está lleno.
passage.native: Luis: No, the reservoir is full.

passage.target: Luis: El cofre está abierto y un faro está roto.
passage.native: Luis: The hood is open and a headlight is broken.

passage.target: Luis: La batería es nueva y está limpia.
passage.native: Luis: The battery is new and it is clean.

example.target: Es una troca Ford.
example.native: It's a Ford truck.

verbs.note: Irregular. Use ser for what something is: its identity, type, brand or a lasting trait like new.

example.target: El aceite está bajo.
example.native: The oil is low.

verbs.note: Irregular. Use estar for a condition (low, loose, worn, dirty) or a location (on the lift).

example.target: Luis revisa la troca en el elevador.
example.native: Luis checks the truck on the lift.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, need and want, what there is, and what you must do in the shop.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Tell a coworker what tools you need, what the customer wants, and what everyone has to wear in the shop.

items.note: Mexican usage; other regions say el destornillador.
Mexican usage; many US shops also say la parte.

items.native: Do you have the car keys?

items.target: Hay un ruido en la llanta delantera.
items.native: There's a noise in the front tire.
items.note: hay: there is / there are.

items.target: La clienta quiere un cambio de aceite.
items.native: The customer wants an oil change.
items.note: A woman is la clienta; a man is el cliente.

items.target: Hay que usar lentes de seguridad.
items.native: You have to wear safety glasses.
items.note: hay que + infinitive: something everyone must do.

passage.target: En el Taller Díaz, la señora Ramos necesita un foco.
passage.native: At the Díaz Shop, Mrs. Ramos needs a bulb.

passage.target: Ana: ¿Tiene usted las llaves del carro?
passage.native: Ana: Do you have the car keys?

passage.target: Señora Ramos: Sí, pero el carro tiene poca gasolina.
passage.native: Mrs. Ramos: Yes, but the car has little gas.

passage.target: Ana: Luis, la clienta también quiere un cambio de aceite.
passage.native: Ana: Luis, the customer also wants an oil change.

passage.target: Ana: Hay un ruido en la llanta delantera.
passage.native: Ana: There's a noise in the front tire.

passage.target: Ana: Necesito la llave de cruz y las pinzas, por favor.
passage.native: Ana: I need the lug wrench and the pliers, please.

passage.target: Luis: Aquí están, y hay un trapo limpio en la mesa.
passage.native: Luis: Here they are, and there is a clean rag on the table.

passage.target: Luis: Ya tenemos la refacción, y aquí está el desarmador.
passage.native: Luis: We already have the part, and here is the screwdriver.

passage.target: Luis: Hay que usar lentes de seguridad y guantes.
passage.native: Luis: You have to wear safety glasses and gloves.

example.target: ¿Tiene usted las llaves del carro?
example.native: Do you have the car keys?

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (tengo). Stem change e to ie (tienes, tiene, tienen), except nosotros. Use tiene with usted for a customer.

example.target: Necesito la llave de cruz y las pinzas, por favor.
example.native: I need the lug wrench and the pliers, please.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Put the thing you need right after it.

example.target: La clienta también quiere un cambio de aceite.
example.native: The customer also wants an oil change.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (quiero, quieres), except nosotros.

example.target: En el taller, usamos lentes de seguridad.
example.native: In the shop, we wear safety glasses.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Hay que usar means everyone has to wear or use something. Hay means there is or there are, and it never changes.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you're going to do, and what you can do in the shop.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Tell the shop foreman where you are going, what you are going to do today, and what you can do tomorrow.

items.note: Mexican usage; can mean now or in a little while.

items.target: Voy a la tienda de refacciones.
items.native: I'm going to the parts store.

items.target: Voy a revisar los frenos hoy.
items.native: I'm going to check the brakes today.
items.note: ir a + infinitive: a plan.

items.native: Can I move your car to the parking lot?

items.target: Ella va a esperar en la sala de espera.
items.native: She's going to wait in the waiting room.

passage.target: Hoy Luis trabaja en el Taller Ramírez con su jefe, Don Pedro.
passage.native: Today Luis works at Taller Ramírez with his boss, Don Pedro.

passage.target: La señora Ortiz llega a la oficina con un problema de frenos.
passage.native: Mrs. Ortiz arrives at the office with a brake problem.

passage.target: Luis: ¿Puedo mover su carro al estacionamiento?
passage.native: Luis: Can I move your car to the parking lot?

passage.target: Ella va a esperar en la sala de espera.
passage.native: She's going to wait in the waiting room.

passage.target: Luis le dice a Don Pedro: Voy a revisar los frenos hoy.
passage.native: Luis tells Don Pedro: I'm going to check the brakes today.

passage.target: Luis: Ahorita voy a la tienda de refacciones por las balatas.
passage.native: Luis: Right now I'm going to the parts store for the brake pads.

passage.target: Luis: Después del almuerzo, voy a quitar las llantas con la pistola de impacto.
passage.native: Luis: After lunch, I'm going to take off the wheels with the impact gun.

passage.target: Luis: Mañana traigo mi caja de herramientas y puedo ayudar en otros carros.
passage.native: Luis: Tomorrow I'll bring my toolbox and I can help on other cars.

passage.target: Don Pedro: Muy bien, mañana hacemos más trabajos juntos.
passage.native: Don Pedro: Very good, tomorrow we'll do more jobs together.

example.target: Ahorita voy a la tienda de refacciones por las balatas.
example.native: Right now I'm going to the parts store for the brake pads.

verbs.note: Irregular verb. Use ir a + infinitive for plans: voy a revisar = I'm going to check.

example.target: Mañana hacemos más trabajos juntos.
example.native: Tomorrow we'll do more jobs together.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: hago. The present tense with mañana can describe a plan for tomorrow.

example.target: ¿Puedo mover su carro al estacionamiento?
example.native: Can I move your car to the parking lot?

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (puedo, puedes), except nosotros (podemos). Follow it with an infinitive. Su carro is the formal usted form for a customer.

example.target: Ella va a esperar en la sala de espera.
example.native: She's going to wait in the waiting room.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. After va a, use the infinitive: va a esperar.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Describe everyday shop tasks in the present tense with yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Tell a coworker what you do each day in the shop, and ask what they check on a car.

items.note: Common shop word for an engine belt.
-ar verbs: cambio, cambias, cambia, cambiamos, cambian.

items.target: Yo escribo el millaje en el recibo.
items.native: I write the mileage on the receipt.

items.note: tú: informal, between coworkers.

items.target: Usted recoge su carro a las 5.
items.native: You pick up your car at 5.
items.note: usted: formal, for customers.
-ir verbs: abro, abres, abre, abrimos, abren.

passage.target: Luis y Ana abren el Taller Mendoza a las 7.
passage.native: Luis and Ana open Mendoza Shop at 7.

passage.target: Luis: Cada día reviso el tapón del aceite.
passage.native: Luis: Every day I check the oil cap.

passage.native: Luis: I'm changing the belt today.

passage.native: Ana: I cover the seat and the steering wheel with plastic.

passage.target: Ana: Reviso el espejo y escribo las placas en el recibo.
passage.native: Ana: I check the mirror and write the license plates on the receipt.

passage.native: Ana calls Mr. Ortiz: You pick up your car at 5.

example.target: También limpio el parabrisas y subo la ventana.
example.native: I also clean the windshield and roll up the window.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb.

example.target: Yo cambio la banda hoy.
example.native: I'm changing the belt today.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The present tense can also mean what you are doing today.

example.target: Ana escribe las placas en el recibo.
example.native: Ana writes the license plates on the receipt.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb.

example.target: Luis y Ana abren el Taller Mendoza a las 7.
example.native: Luis and Ana open Mendoza Shop at 7.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb.

example.target: Usted recoge su carro a las 5.
example.native: You pick up your car at 5.

verbs.note: Regular -er endings. The yo form is spelled recojo (g changes to j) to keep the same sound.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask customers and coworkers simple questions about a car, its owner, cost and timing.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Ask a customer what problem the car has, when the noise starts, who the owner is, and their phone number.

items.note: It matches the noun: ¿cuántos carros?, ¿cuántas llantas?
Two words in questions; porque (one word) means because.
Use ¿cuál es...? for 'what is' a name or number.

items.native: What problem does your car have?
How much does the oil change cost?
Who is the owner of the car?

passage.native: Carlos greets Mrs. Ruiz at the shop: How are you?

example.native: What problem does your car have?

example.native: When does the noise start?

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (empiezo, empiezas), except nosotros.

example.target: ¿Quién es el dueño del carro?
example.native: Who is the owner of the car?

verbs.note: Irregular. Use ser for who someone is, phone numbers and prices.

example.target: La luz del tablero está prendida.
example.native: The dashboard light is on.

verbs.note: Use estar for conditions and locations: ¿Dónde están las llaves?

example.target: ¿Cuánto cuesta la revisión?
example.native: How much does the inspection cost?

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (cuesta, cuestan), except nosotros. Mostly used as cuesta and cuestan.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody, nothing and not yet, and compare with more, less and another.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Tell a customer their car isn't ready yet, that you see no leak under it, and that another tire costs less.

items.note: After a verb, keep no: No veo nada.
Never use un before otro: otro trapo.

items.target: Su carro todavía no está listo.
No hay nadie en la oficina.
Nunca trabajo debajo del carro sin soportes de seguridad.
items.native: I never work under the car without jack stands.
items.note: Some shops call jack stands las torres.

items.target: No veo nada debajo del carro.
items.native: I don't see anything under the car.

passage.native: Mrs. Ramírez comes to the shop again.

passage.native: There's nobody in the office, and Luis helps her.

passage.native: Luis: Your car isn't ready yet.

passage.native: Luis: I never work under the car without jack stands.

passage.target: Luis: No veo nada debajo del carro.
passage.native: Luis: I don't see anything under the car.

passage.target: Luis: No hay ninguna fuga de aceite.
passage.native: Luis: There is no oil leak.

example.target: Su carro todavía no está listo.

example.target: No veo nada debajo del carro.

example.target: Nunca trabajo debajo del carro sin soportes de seguridad.
example.native: I never work under the car without jack stands.

verbs.native: to help (a customer), to attend to

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Make polite requests and give simple usted commands to customers at the shop.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Ask a customer politely to turn off the engine, put on the parking brake, and sign at the counter.

items.native: Can you turn off the engine, please?
items.note: ¿Puede + infinitive? is a polite request to one person.

items.target: Ponga el freno de mano, por favor.

items.native: Can you give me your name?

example.target: Ponga el freno de mano, por favor.

example.target: ¿Puede apagar el motor, por favor?
example.native: Can you turn off the engine, please?

verbs.native: to come in, to go (to a place)

example.native: Please come to the counter.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The usted command is pase.

example.target: Firme aquí, por favor.
example.native: Sign here, please.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize shop cognates and use survival phrases to get help when you don't understand.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Tell a coworker you speak a little Spanish, ask them to repeat more slowly, and ask how to say a part in Spanish.

items.note: -ción words are feminine: la inspección.
-dad words are feminine and match English -ty.
A woman is la clienta.

items.native: I don't understand, can you repeat?
How do you say 'lug nut' in Spanish?
I need help with the repair.

passage.target: El radiador de un cliente está dañado por un accidente.
passage.native: A customer's radiator is damaged from an accident.

passage.target: El cliente da información: se calienta a alta velocidad.
passage.native: The customer gives information: it overheats at high speed.

passage.native: Rosa and Kevin do the inspection today.

passage.native: Kevin: I speak a little Spanish.

lessons.title: Explain the Charging System to a New Lube Tech
lessons.objective: Explain step by step how the battery, alternator and belt work together and why the battery light comes on.
lessons.explanation:
Connectors for sequence and cause (primero el motor gira la banda, luego el alternador carga, por eso se enciende la luz)
Primero el motor gira la banda y luego el alternador produce corriente. — First the engine turns the belt and then the alternator produces current.
El alternador no estaba cargando, por eso se encendió la luz de la batería. — The alternator wasn't charging, so the battery light came on.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the lead tech, and the AI is Tomás, a new lube tech: explain step by step how the battery, alternator and belt work together, using primero, luego, después and por eso, then have him explain it back and correct him kindly.

items.note: Mexican shops say corriente directa (CD); you may also hear corriente continua.
Agrees with la batería: la batería está descargada.

items.target: Primero el motor gira la banda, luego la banda mueve el alternador.
items.native: First the engine turns the belt, then the belt drives the alternator.

items.target: El alternador carga la batería mientras el motor está encendido.
items.native: The alternator charges the battery while the engine is running.

items.target: Si la banda se rompe, el alternador ya no carga.
items.native: If the belt breaks, the alternator stops charging.

items.target: Por eso se enciende la luz de la batería.
items.native: That's why the battery light comes on.

items.target: La batería arranca el carro; el alternador la mantiene cargada.
items.native: The battery starts the car; the alternator keeps it charged.

items.target: Por lo tanto, una batería nueva no arregla un alternador malo.
items.native: So a new battery doesn't fix a bad alternator.

items.target: No te preocupes, mucha gente los confunde.
items.native: Don't worry, a lot of people mix them up.
items.note: Informal tú, coworker to coworker.

items.target: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso a paso.
items.native: Now you explain it to me, step by step.
items.note: Informal tú.

passage.target: En un taller de cambio de aceite de la Ruta 9, Andrea Morales le explica el sistema de carga a Tomás Rivera.
passage.native: At a quick-lube on Route 9, Andrea Morales explains the charging system to Tomás Rivera.

passage.target: Tomás es nuevo y esta mañana le dijo a una clienta que la batería cargaba el alternador.
passage.native: Tomás is new, and this morning he told a customer that the battery charged the alternator.

passage.target: Andrea: No te preocupes, mucha gente los confunde.
passage.native: Andrea: Don't worry, a lot of people mix them up.

passage.target: Andrea abre el cofre y le muestra la polea del cigüeñal, que gira con el motor y mueve la banda serpentina.
passage.native: Andrea opens the hood and shows him the crankshaft pulley, which turns with the engine and drives the serpentine belt.

passage.target: Andrea: Primero el motor gira la banda, luego la banda mueve el alternador.
passage.native: Andrea: First the engine turns the belt, then the belt drives the alternator.

passage.target: Andrea: Dentro del alternador se produce corriente alterna, pero la batería no la puede usar.
passage.native: Andrea: Inside the alternator, alternating current is produced, but the battery can't use it.

passage.target: Andrea: Por eso los diodos la convierten en corriente directa antes de mandarla a la batería.
passage.native: Andrea: That's why the diodes convert it to direct current before sending it to the battery.

passage.target: Andrea: Después el regulador de voltaje controla cuánto carga el alternador para no sobrecargar la batería.
passage.native: Andrea: After that, the voltage regulator controls how much the alternator charges so it doesn't overcharge the battery.

passage.target: Andrea: La batería arranca el carro; el alternador la mantiene cargada.
passage.native: Andrea: The battery starts the car; the alternator keeps it charged.

passage.target: Andrea: Si la banda se rompe, el alternador ya no carga.
passage.native: Andrea: If the belt breaks, the alternator stops charging.

passage.target: Andrea: Por eso se enciende la luz de la batería.
passage.native: Andrea: That's why the battery light comes on.

passage.target: Andrea: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso a paso.
passage.native: Andrea: Now you explain it to me, step by step.

passage.target: Tomás: Primero el cigüeñal gira la banda serpentina, luego la banda mueve el alternador y después la batería carga el alternador.
passage.native: Tomás: First the crankshaft turns the serpentine belt, then the belt drives the alternator, and after that the battery charges the alternator.

passage.target: Andrea: Muy bien, solo cambia el último paso, porque el alternador carga la batería mientras el motor está encendido.
passage.native: Andrea: Very good, just change the last step, because the alternator charges the battery while the engine is running.

passage.target: Después Tomás revisa la tensión de la banda en el carro de la clienta y la encuentra bien.
passage.native: Next, Tomás checks the belt tension on the customer's car and finds it okay.

passage.target: Luego conecta el probador de baterías y la pantalla dice que la batería está descargada.
passage.native: Then he connects the battery tester, and the screen says the battery is dead.

passage.target: Antes de cambiar nada, Tomás limpia la corrosión del borne positivo con un cepillo de terminales.
passage.native: Before replacing anything, Tomás cleans the corrosion off the positive post with a terminal brush.

passage.target: Andrea: Si el cable de tierra está bien apretado y la batería se vuelve a descargar, buscamos un consumo parásito.
passage.native: Andrea: If the ground cable is tight and the battery goes dead again, we look for a parasitic draw.

example.target: Andrea le explica el sistema de carga a Tomás.
example.native: Andrea explains the charging system to Tomás.

example.native: First the engine turns the belt.

example.native: The alternator charges the battery while the engine is running.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The opposite is descargar; a dead battery is una batería descargada.

example.target: Por eso se enciende la luz de la batería.
example.native: That's why the battery light comes on.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (enciendo, enciendes), except nosotros. Use the reflexive form for a light coming on by itself.

lessons.title: Why We Torque Lug Nuts in a Star Pattern
lessons.objective: Explain why lug nuts are tightened in a star pattern with a torque wrench to the value the manufacturer specifies.
lessons.explanation:
Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se aprieta en estrella; si se aprieta en círculo, el rotor se deforma)
Las tuercas se aprietan en estrella con la llave de torque. — The lug nuts are tightened in a star pattern with the torque wrench.
Si se aprietan solo con la pistola, el rotor se puede deformar. — If they're tightened only with the impact gun, the rotor can warp.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the senior tire tech, and the AI is Yesenia, an apprentice: explain why the impact gun alone isn't enough and why we tighten in a star pattern, using se aprieta and si + present, then have her read the torque value from the manufacturer's chart.

items.note: Mexican shop term; some techs also use birlo loosely for the lug nut.
Written lb-pie; US shops use foot-pounds.
Common Mexican usage for the metal wheel.
Common in Mexico for the wheel hub.

items.target: Las tuercas se aprietan en estrella, nunca en círculo.
items.native: Lug nuts are tightened in a star pattern, never in a circle.

items.target: Si se aprietan en círculo, el rin no asienta parejo.
items.native: If they're tightened in a circle, the wheel doesn't seat evenly.

items.target: Primero se ponen a mano, luego se usa la llave de torque.
items.native: First you start them by hand, then you use the torque wrench.

items.target: La pistola de impacto no da el torque exacto.
items.native: The impact gun doesn't give the exact torque.

items.target: ¿Qué valor de torque da la tabla del fabricante?
items.native: What torque value does the manufacturer's chart give?

items.target: Léeme el valor de la tabla para esta camioneta.
items.native: Read me the value from the chart for this SUV.
items.note: Informal tú, to an apprentice.

items.target: Si suena el clic, se deja de apretar.
items.native: If it clicks, you stop tightening.

items.target: Si una tuerca no da el clic, avísame.
items.native: If a nut doesn't click, let me know.
items.note: Informal tú.

passage.target: En la llantera Ruiz Tires de San Antonio, Rogelio Medina le enseña a la aprendiz Yesenia Flores a montar las ruedas en la camioneta de una clienta.
passage.native: At Ruiz Tires, a tire shop in San Antonio, Rogelio Medina is teaching apprentice Yesenia Flores to mount the wheels on a customer's SUV.

passage.target: La camioneta ya tiene llantas nuevas, y Yesenia quiere apretar cada tuerca de rueda solo con la pistola de impacto.
passage.native: The SUV already has new tires, and Yesenia wants to tighten each lug nut with only the impact gun.

passage.target: Rogelio: La pistola de impacto no da el torque exacto.
passage.native: Rogelio: The impact gun doesn't give the exact torque.

passage.target: Rogelio: Si se aprietan de más con la pistola, la rosca del birlo se puede dañar.
passage.native: Rogelio: If they're overtightened with the gun, the threads on the wheel stud can get damaged.

passage.target: Rogelio: Primero se ponen a mano, luego se usa la llave de torque.
passage.native: Rogelio: First you start them by hand, then you use the torque wrench.

passage.target: Yesenia pone cada tuerca a mano, y así el asiento de la tuerca entra centrado en el rin.
passage.native: Yesenia starts each nut by hand, and that way the nut seat goes in centered on the wheel.

passage.target: Rogelio: Las tuercas se aprietan en estrella, nunca en círculo.
passage.native: Rogelio: Lug nuts are tightened in a star pattern, never in a circle.

passage.target: Yesenia le pregunta por qué importa tanto el patrón en estrella.
passage.native: Yesenia asks him why the star pattern matters so much.

passage.target: Rogelio: Si se aprietan en círculo, el rin no asienta parejo.
passage.native: Rogelio: If they're tightened in a circle, the wheel doesn't seat evenly.

passage.target: Rogelio: Si el rin no queda plano contra la maza, el rotor sufre una deformación y el pedal del freno vibra.
passage.native: Rogelio: If the wheel doesn't sit flat against the hub, the rotor suffers warping and the brake pedal vibrates.

passage.target: Yesenia: ¿Qué valor de torque da la tabla del fabricante?
passage.native: Yesenia: What torque value does the manufacturer's chart give?

passage.target: Rogelio: Léeme el valor de la tabla para esta camioneta.
passage.native: Rogelio: Read me the value from the chart for this SUV.

passage.target: Yesenia busca el modelo en la tabla de torque del fabricante y lee el valor en voz alta: 140 libras-pie.
passage.native: Yesenia looks up the model in the manufacturer's torque chart and reads the value out loud: 140 foot-pounds.

passage.target: Rogelio ajusta la llave de torque a 140 libras-pie, como indica la tabla, y Yesenia confirma el número.
passage.native: Rogelio sets the torque wrench to 140 foot-pounds, as the chart indicates, and Yesenia confirms the number.

passage.target: Rogelio: Si suena el clic, se deja de apretar.
passage.native: Rogelio: If it clicks, you stop tightening.

passage.target: Yesenia aprieta cada tuerca de rueda en estrella hasta oír el clic de la llave, y luego repite el patrón para revisar.
passage.native: Yesenia tightens each lug nut in a star pattern until she hears the click of the wrench, and then repeats the pattern to check.

passage.target: Rogelio: Si una tuerca no da el clic, avísame.
passage.native: Rogelio: If a nut doesn't click, let me know.

passage.target: Todas las tuercas dan el clic, y Rogelio anota el valor de torque en la orden de trabajo de la clienta.
passage.native: All the nuts click, and Rogelio writes the torque value on the customer's work order.

example.native: Lug nuts are tightened in a star pattern, never in a circle.

example.native: Yesenia starts each nut by hand.

example.native: Read me the value from the chart for this SUV.

example.target: Si suena el clic, se deja de apretar.
example.native: If it clicks, you stop tightening.

example.target: Si una tuerca no da el clic, avísame.
example.native: If a nut doesn't click, let me know.

lessons.title: Training a New Tech on Lift Point Placement
lessons.objective: Coach a new tech through setting a two-post lift on the manufacturer's lift points and have them teach it back.
lessons.explanation:
Commands with object pronouns (colócalo en el punto marcado, súbelo un poco, sacúdelo, no lo subas más todavía)
Colócalo en el punto marcado y súbelo un poco. — Put it on the marked point and raise it a little.
No lo subas más todavía; primero sacúdelo. — Don't raise it any higher yet; shake it first.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the lead tech, and the AI is Brayan, a new hire: walk him through checking the lift guide and setting the two-post lift on this sedan's lift points with commands like colócalo, súbelo and no lo subas todavía, then have him teach it back.

items.note: Many techs also just say unibody.
Common US Spanish loanword; informal shop talk.

items.target: Este carro no es como la troca de ayer.
items.native: This car isn't like the truck from yesterday.

items.target: Antes de subirlo, revisa la guía de elevación.
items.native: Before you raise it, check the lifting guide.
items.note: Informal tú, to a new hire.

items.target: Colócala en el punto marcado, sobre la pestaña.
items.native: Put it (the pad) on the marked point, on the pinch weld.
Raise it a little and stop.

items.target: Sacúdelo con cuidado para ver si está firme.
items.native: Shake it carefully to see if it's stable.
Don't raise it any higher yet.

items.target: Si tienes duda, no lo levantes; pregúntame.
items.native: If you're unsure, don't lift it; ask me.

items.target: Ahora enséñamelo tú, como si yo fuera nuevo.
items.native: Now you show me, as if I were new.

passage.target: En el Taller Ramírez, Héctor Ramírez entrena a Brayan Morales, un técnico nuevo, en el elevador de dos postes.
passage.native: At Ramírez Auto Repair, Héctor Ramírez trains Brayan Morales, a new tech, on the two-post lift.

passage.target: Hoy van a subir un sedán de carrocería monocasco, pero ayer Brayan subió una troca grande.
passage.native: Today they are going to lift a unibody sedan, but yesterday Brayan lifted a big pickup truck.

passage.target: Héctor: Este carro no es como la troca de ayer.
passage.native: Héctor: This car isn't like the truck from yesterday.

passage.target: Héctor: Antes de subirlo, revisa la guía de elevación.
passage.native: Héctor: Before you raise it, check the lifting guide.

passage.target: Según la guía del fabricante, los puntos de elevación de este sedán están en la pestaña de soldadura, debajo de las puertas.
passage.native: According to the manufacturer's guide, this sedan's lift points are on the pinch weld, under the doors.

passage.target: Héctor explica que en la troca usaron el adaptador de altura, pero aquí la guía no lo pide.
passage.native: Héctor explains that on the truck they used the height adapter, but here the guide doesn't call for it.

passage.target: Héctor: Gira los brazos del elevador debajo del carro, pero no los acerques a las líneas de freno.
passage.native: Héctor: Swing the lift arms under the car, but don't bring them close to the brake lines.

passage.target: Héctor explica que una almohadilla mal puesta puede aplastar una línea o abollar el tanque de gasolina.
passage.native: Héctor explains that a badly placed pad can crush a line or dent the fuel tank.

passage.target: Héctor le da la primera almohadilla a Brayan y le dice: Colócala en el punto marcado, sobre la pestaña.
passage.native: Héctor hands Brayan the first pad and tells him: Put it on the marked point, on the pinch weld.

passage.target: Brayan coloca las otras almohadillas, y Héctor se agacha para ver que todas queden parejas.
passage.native: Brayan places the other pads, and Héctor crouches down to check that they all sit level.

passage.target: Héctor: Según la guía, el centro de gravedad está más adelante, por el motor, así que céntralo bien entre los postes.
passage.native: Héctor: According to the guide, the center of gravity is farther forward, by the engine, so center it well between the posts.

passage.target: Héctor: Súbelo un poco y detente.
passage.native: Héctor: Raise it a little and stop.

passage.target: Con las llantas apenas despegadas del piso, Héctor dice: Sacúdelo con cuidado para ver si está firme.
passage.native: With the tires barely off the floor, Héctor says: Shake it carefully to see if it's stable.

passage.target: Brayan empuja el carro y se mueve un poco, así que Héctor le dice: No lo subas más todavía; bájalo y ajusta las almohadillas.
passage.native: Brayan pushes the car and it moves a little, so Héctor tells him: Don't raise it any higher yet; lower it and adjust the pads.

passage.target: Luego Brayan ajusta las almohadillas, repite la prueba, sube el carro a la altura de trabajo y lo baja sobre los seguros del elevador.
passage.native: Then Brayan adjusts the pads, repeats the test, raises the car to working height and lowers it onto the lift locks.

passage.target: Héctor: Si tienes duda, no lo levantes; pregúntame.
passage.native: Héctor: If you're unsure, don't lift it; ask me.

passage.target: Héctor: Ahora enséñamelo tú, como si yo fuera nuevo.
passage.native: Héctor: Now you show me, as if I were new.

passage.target: Brayan se lo explica paso por paso: Revisa la guía, coloca las almohadillas en los puntos marcados, súbelo un poco y sacúdelo.
passage.native: Brayan explains it to him step by step: Check the guide, put the pads on the marked points, raise it a little and shake it.

example.native: Before you raise it, check the lifting guide.

example.target: Súbelo un poco y detente.

example.target: Sacúdelo con cuidado para ver si está firme.
example.native: Shake it carefully to see if it's stable.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb. Command with a pronoun: sacúdelo, with an accent on the stressed syllable.

example.target: Ahora enséñamelo tú, como si yo fuera nuevo.
example.native: Now you show me, as if I were new.

lessons.title: Read the Hybrid Shutdown Procedure Before You Touch
lessons.objective: Read the manufacturer's high-voltage shutdown procedure aloud and explain each step, including testing before touching.
lessons.explanation:

Antes de desconectar la clavija, hay que apagar el carro y alejar la llave inteligente. — Before disconnecting the service plug, you have to turn off the car and move the smart key away.
Después de esperar el tiempo que indica el fabricante, hay que medir el voltaje residual. — After waiting the time the manufacturer specifies, you have to measure the residual voltage.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the lead hybrid tech, and the AI is Lucía, a second-year tech: read the manufacturer's high-voltage shutdown procedure aloud and explain each step, including testing with the meter before touching, using antes de, después de and hay que.

items.note: Orange cables mark high voltage on hybrids.
Test the meter on a known live source before and after measuring.
Opposite of energizado; agrees with the noun: el circuito desenergizado.

items.target: Antes de quitar la tapa, hay que confirmar con el multímetro.
items.native: Before removing the cover, we have to confirm with the meter.

items.target: Hay que esperar el tiempo que indica el fabricante.
items.native: We have to wait the time the manufacturer specifies.

items.target: Lee el paso 3 en voz alta, por favor.
items.note: Informal tú, to a coworker.

items.target: Antes de tocar nada, revisa tus guantes aislantes.

items.target: Después de quitar la clavija, guárdala en un lugar seguro.

passage.target: En Híbridos del Valle, en San Antonio, Daniel Ortiz y Lucía Paredes revisan un híbrido con fuga de anticongelante cerca del inversor.
passage.native: At Híbridos del Valle, in San Antonio, Daniel Ortiz and Lucía Paredes are checking a hybrid with a coolant leak near the inverter.

passage.target: Daniel abre el procedimiento de apagado del fabricante y le pide a Lucía que lea y explique cada paso.
passage.native: Daniel opens the manufacturer's shutdown procedure and asks Lucía to read and explain each step.

passage.target: Lucía lee el paso 1: Antes de desconectar nada, hay que apagar el carro con el botón de encendido y alejar la llave inteligente.
passage.native: Lucía reads step 1: Before disconnecting anything, you have to turn off the car with the power button and move the smart key away.

passage.target: Daniel explica que con la llave inteligente lejos, nadie puede encender el sistema por accidente.
passage.native: Daniel explains that with the smart key far away, nobody can turn on the system by accident.

passage.target: Después de apagar el carro, Lucía pone el bloqueo y etiquetado y cuelga el letrero de advertencia en el volante.
passage.native: After turning off the car, Lucía applies lockout/tagout and hangs the warning sign on the steering wheel.

passage.target: Daniel: Lee el paso 3 en voz alta, por favor.
passage.native: Daniel: Read step 3 out loud, please.

passage.target: Lucía lee: Con los guantes aislantes puestos, quite la clavija de servicio.
passage.native: Lucía reads: With the insulated gloves on, remove the service plug.

passage.target: Daniel: Antes de tocar nada, revisa tus guantes aislantes.
passage.native: Daniel: Before touching anything, check your insulated gloves.

passage.target: Lucía revisa los guantes con aire, no encuentra ninguna fuga y quita la clavija de servicio con cuidado.
passage.native: Lucía checks the gloves with air, finds no leak, and carefully removes the service plug.

passage.target: Daniel: Después de quitar la clavija, guárdala en un lugar seguro.
passage.native: Daniel: After removing the service plug, keep it in a safe place.

passage.target: Lucía: El anticongelante sigue goteando, así que mejor quitamos la tapa del inversor ahorita, ¿no?
passage.native: Lucía: The coolant is still dripping, so we'd better take off the inverter cover right now, right?

passage.target: Daniel: No nos saltamos ningún paso del procedimiento.
passage.native: Daniel: We don't skip any step of the procedure.

passage.target: Según el manual del fabricante, el tiempo de espera es de 10 minutos para que los capacitores se descarguen.
passage.native: According to the manufacturer's manual, the waiting time is 10 minutes so the capacitors can discharge.

passage.target: Daniel: Hasta que confirmemos, nadie toca los cables naranjas.
passage.native: Daniel: Until we confirm, nobody touches the orange cables.

passage.target: Después de esperar el tiempo completo, Daniel dice: Primero pruebo el multímetro en una fuente conocida.
passage.native: After waiting the full time, Daniel says: First I test the meter on a known source.

passage.target: La lectura en la fuente conocida confirma que el multímetro y las puntas de prueba funcionan bien.
passage.native: The reading on the known source confirms that the meter and the test leads work properly.

passage.target: Daniel: Antes de quitar la tapa, hay que confirmar con el multímetro.
passage.native: Daniel: Before removing the cover, we have to confirm with the meter.

passage.target: Daniel mide el voltaje residual donde indica el manual, la lectura es de 0 voltios y el sistema está desenergizado.
passage.native: Daniel measures the residual voltage where the manual indicates, the reading is 0 volts, and the system is de-energized.

example.target: Lucía quita la clavija de servicio con cuidado.
example.native: Lucía carefully removes the service plug.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In manuals you will see the formal command quite (remove).

example.target: Esperamos el tiempo completo antes de medir.
example.native: We wait the full time before measuring.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Takes a direct object with no preposition: esperar el tiempo (to wait the time).

example.target: Daniel mide el voltaje residual.
example.native: Daniel measures the residual voltage.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (mido, mides), except nosotros.

example.target: Primero pruebo el multímetro en una fuente conocida.
example.native: First I test the meter on a known source.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (pruebo, pruebas), except nosotros.

example.target: Lucía cuelga el letrero de advertencia en el volante.
example.native: Lucía hangs the warning sign on the steering wheel.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (cuelgo, cuelgas), except nosotros.

lessons.title: Snapped Manifold Stud: Telling the Waiting Customer
lessons.objective: Explain to a customer how a rusted exhaust stud broke during the job and propose two repair options with cost and time.
lessons.explanation:
Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (el perno estaba muy oxidado y se rompió; podríamos extraerlo o cambiaríamos el múltiple)
El espárrago estaba muy oxidado y se rompió al aflojarlo. — The stud was very rusted and broke when I loosened it.
Podríamos extraerlo hoy o cambiaríamos el múltiple completo mañana. — We could extract it today, or we would replace the whole manifold tomorrow.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the technician, and the AI is Don Ernesto Salgado, waiting in the lobby for his pickup: explain how the rusted stud broke with preterite and imperfect (estaba oxidado, se rompió), then offer two options with cost and time using the conditional (podríamos, tardaría).

items.note: A headless threaded stud; many shops also call it perno.
Mexican shops say empaque; junta is also heard.
Mexican shop term for a thread-cutting tap.
Agrees with the noun: el espárrago oxidado, la tuerca oxidada.

items.target: Don Ernesto, disculpe, tengo que explicarle algo de su camioneta.
items.native: Don Ernesto, excuse me, I need to explain something about your truck.
items.note: Formal: Don + first name shows respect to an older customer.

items.target: El espárrago estaba muy oxidado y se rompió.
items.native: The stud was very rusted and it broke.

items.target: Mientras lo aflojaba, se quebró dentro de la cabeza.
items.native: While I was loosening it, it snapped inside the head.

items.target: Podríamos extraerlo hoy, pero tardaría unas 2 horas más.
items.native: We could extract it today, but it would take about 2 more hours.

items.target: La otra opción sería cambiar el múltiple con espárragos nuevos.
items.native: The other option would be to replace the manifold with new studs.

items.target: Con esa opción, su camioneta estaría lista mañana.
items.native: With that option, your truck would be ready tomorrow.

items.note: Formal.

items.target: Oye, pásame el soplete y el aceite penetrante.
items.native: Hey, hand me the torch and the penetrating oil.
items.note: Informal, to a coworker in the bay.

passage.target: En el Taller Hermanos Ruiz, Ramiro cambiaba el empaque del múltiple de la camioneta vieja de Don Ernesto Salgado.
passage.native: At Hermanos Ruiz Shop, Ramiro was replacing the manifold gasket on Don Ernesto Salgado's old pickup.

passage.target: El múltiple de escape tenía una fuga, y Don Ernesto esperaba en la sala con un café.
passage.native: The exhaust manifold had a leak, and Don Ernesto was waiting in the lobby with a coffee.

passage.target: Ramiro le dijo a su compañero Beto: Oye, pásame el soplete y el aceite penetrante.
passage.native: Ramiro said to his coworker Beto: Hey, hand me the torch and the penetrating oil.

passage.target: Ramiro calentó la zona y esperó unos minutos, pero los espárragos estaban muy oxidados.
passage.native: Ramiro heated the area and waited a few minutes, but the studs were very rusted.

passage.target: Mientras aflojaba el último espárrago, este se quebró y el pedazo roto se quedó dentro de la cabeza de cilindros.
passage.native: While he was loosening the last stud, it snapped and the broken piece stayed inside the cylinder head.

passage.target: Ramiro se limpió las manos y fue a la sala de espera para hablar con el cliente.
passage.native: Ramiro wiped his hands and went to the waiting room to talk with the customer.

passage.target: Ramiro: Don Ernesto, disculpe, tengo que explicarle algo de su camioneta.
passage.native: Ramiro: Don Ernesto, excuse me, I need to explain something about your truck.

passage.target: Ramiro: El espárrago estaba muy oxidado y se rompió.
passage.native: Ramiro: The stud was very rusted and it broke.

passage.target: Ramiro: Mientras lo aflojaba, se quebró dentro de la cabeza.
passage.native: Ramiro: While I was loosening it, it snapped inside the head.

passage.target: Ramiro: Para sacarlo, primero haría un agujero en el centro con el taladro y una broca pequeña.
passage.native: Ramiro: To get it out, I would first make a hole in the center with the drill and a small drill bit.

passage.target: Ramiro: Después usaría el extractor de espárragos y limpiaría la rosca con un machuelo.
passage.native: Ramiro: Then I would use the stud extractor and clean the threads with a tap.

passage.target: Ramiro: Podríamos extraerlo hoy, pero tardaría unas 2 horas más.
passage.native: Ramiro: We could extract it today, but it would take about 2 more hours.

passage.target: Ramiro: El costo adicional sería de 180 dólares, según el presupuesto de la oficina.
passage.native: Ramiro: The additional cost would be 180 dollars, according to the office's estimate.

passage.target: Ramiro: La otra opción sería cambiar el múltiple con espárragos nuevos.
passage.native: Ramiro: The other option would be to replace the manifold with new studs.

passage.target: Ramiro: Con esa opción, su camioneta estaría lista mañana.
passage.native: Ramiro: With that option, your truck would be ready tomorrow.

passage.target: Ramiro: El tiempo estimado sería de 4 horas y costaría 450 dólares con la pieza, según el presupuesto.
passage.native: Ramiro: The estimated time would be 4 hours and it would cost 450 dollars with the part, according to the estimate.

passage.target: Ramiro: ¿Cuál opción prefiere usted?
passage.native: Ramiro: Which option do you prefer?

passage.target: Don Ernesto firmó la autorización para extraerlo hoy porque necesitaba su camioneta para trabajar mañana.
passage.native: Don Ernesto signed the authorization to extract it today because he needed his truck to work tomorrow.

example.target: Este espárrago se rompe fácilmente porque está oxidado.
example.native: This stud breaks easily because it is rusted.

verbs.note: Use the reflexive form when a part breaks on its own: se rompió (preterite) for the moment it broke.

example.target: Aflojo los espárragos despacio después del aceite penetrante.
example.native: I loosen the studs slowly after the penetrating oil.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Imperfect aflojaba describes the action in progress when something broke.

example.target: Extraigo el pedazo roto con el extractor de espárragos.
example.native: I extract the broken piece with the stud extractor.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: extraigo, like traer. Conditional: podríamos extraerlo.

example.target: La reparación tarda unas 2 horas más.
example.native: The repair takes about 2 more hours.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Conditional tardaría gives a time estimate politely.

example.target: ¿Cuál opción prefiere usted?
example.native: Which option do you prefer?

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (prefiero, prefieres), except nosotros. Use prefiere with usted for a customer (formal).

lessons.title: Backordered Water Pump: Offering an Aftermarket Part
lessons.objective: Compare an OEM and an aftermarket water pump by price, warranty and wait time and help the customer choose.
lessons.explanation:
Future and ir a; comparisons (la original va a llegar el lunes; la otra es más barata que la original pero tiene menos garantía)
La original va a llegar el lunes, según el departamento de partes. — The OEM one is going to arrive on Monday, according to the parts department.
La genérica cuesta menos que la original, pero tiene menos garantía. — The aftermarket one costs less than the OEM one, but it has less warranty.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the technician on the service drive, and the AI is Óscar Benítez, a rideshare driver who needs his car tomorrow: compare the OEM and aftermarket water pumps by price, warranty and wait time using ir a, the future and comparisons (más barata que), and help him choose.

items.note: Original means made by the vehicle's maker; US shops also say OEM.
Many US shops also use the loanword aftermarket.
US parts departments also say está en backorder.

items.target: La bomba original no va a llegar hasta el lunes.
items.native: The OEM pump isn't going to arrive until Monday.
items.note: Formal context: speaking to the customer.

items.target: Tenemos otra bomba en existencia, de una marca reconocida.
items.native: We have another pump in stock, from a reputable brand.

items.target: La genérica es más barata que la original.
items.native: The aftermarket one is cheaper than the OEM one.

items.target: Pero su garantía es más corta que la de la original.
items.native: But its warranty is shorter than the OEM one's.

items.target: Si escoge la genérica, tendrá su carro mañana en la tarde.
items.native: If you choose the aftermarket one, you'll have your car tomorrow afternoon.
Do you need the car for work tomorrow?
items.note: Formal (usted implied).

items.target: Le voy a mostrar la garantía por escrito.
items.native: I'm going to show you the warranty in writing.

items.target: Oye, ¿tienes esa bomba en el almacén ahora mismo?
items.native: Hey, do you have that pump in the warehouse right now?
items.note: Informal, to a coworker at the parts counter.

passage.target: El martes en la mañana, el técnico Luis Ramírez atiende a Óscar Benítez en el área de servicio de la agencia.
passage.native: On Tuesday morning, technician Luis Ramírez helps Óscar Benítez in the dealership's service area.

passage.target: Óscar maneja para una aplicación de viajes y ayer vio un goteo de anticongelante debajo del motor.
passage.native: Óscar drives for a rideshare app, and yesterday he saw a drip of coolant under the engine.

passage.target: Luis le explica que el sello de la bomba está roto y que, sin reparación, el sobrecalentamiento puede dañar el motor.
passage.native: Luis explains to him that the pump seal is broken and that, without a repair, the overheating can damage the engine.

passage.target: Luis: ¿Necesita el carro para trabajar mañana?
passage.native: Luis: Do you need the car for work tomorrow?

passage.target: Óscar: Sí, mañana tengo que trabajar desde las 6 de la tarde.
passage.native: Óscar: Yes, tomorrow I have to work starting at 6 in the evening.

passage.target: Luis llama a Rosa, la encargada del departamento de partes, y le pregunta: Oye, ¿tienes esa bomba en el almacén ahora mismo?
passage.native: Luis calls Rosa, the person in charge of the parts department, and asks her: Hey, do you have that pump in the warehouse right now?

passage.target: Rosa revisa la computadora y le contesta que la bomba original está en pedido pendiente con la fábrica.
passage.native: Rosa checks the computer and answers that the OEM pump is on backorder with the factory.

passage.target: Rosa: Según el sistema, la fecha de llegada es el lunes en la mañana.
passage.native: Rosa: According to the system, the arrival date is Monday morning.

passage.target: Luis regresa con Óscar y le dice: La bomba original no va a llegar hasta el lunes.
passage.native: Luis goes back to Óscar and tells him: The OEM pump isn't going to arrive until Monday.

passage.target: Luis: Tenemos otra bomba en existencia, de una marca reconocida.
passage.native: Luis: We have another pump in stock, from a reputable brand.

passage.target: Luis: La pieza genérica cuesta 280 dólares y la original 410, así que la diferencia de precio es de 130 dólares.
passage.native: Luis: The aftermarket part costs 280 dollars and the OEM one 410, so the price difference is 130 dollars.

passage.target: Luis: Pero su garantía es más corta que la de la original.
passage.native: Luis: But its warranty is shorter than the OEM one's.

passage.target: Luis: Según la hoja del fabricante, la genérica tiene una garantía limitada de 12 meses y la original tiene una de 24 meses.
passage.native: Luis: According to the manufacturer's sheet, the aftermarket one has a limited warranty of 12 months and the OEM one has one of 24 months.

passage.target: Luis: Le voy a mostrar la garantía por escrito.
passage.native: Luis: I'm going to show you the warranty in writing.

passage.target: Óscar pregunta si la agencia le puede prestar un carro de cortesía hasta el lunes.
passage.native: Óscar asks if the dealership can lend him a loaner car until Monday.

passage.target: Luis: Lo siento, hoy no tenemos ningún carro de cortesía disponible.
passage.native: Luis: I'm sorry, today we don't have any loaner car available.

passage.target: Luis: Si escoge la genérica, tendrá su carro mañana en la tarde.
passage.native: Luis: If you choose the aftermarket one, you'll have your car tomorrow afternoon.

passage.target: Óscar lee la garantía por escrito y decide: Voy a escoger la genérica, porque no puedo perder tantos días de trabajo.
passage.native: Óscar reads the warranty in writing and decides: I'm going to choose the aftermarket one, because I can't lose so many days of work.

example.target: La bomba original llega el lunes.
example.native: The OEM pump arrives on Monday.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use ir a + llegar for a planned arrival (va a llegar).

example.target: Tenemos otra bomba en existencia.
example.native: We have another pump in stock.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (tengo); stem change e to ie (tienes), except nosotros. Future: tendrá.

example.target: La pieza genérica cuesta 280 dólares.
example.native: The aftermarket part costs 280 dollars.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (cuesta, cuestan), except nosotros. With parts, you mostly use cuesta and cuestan.

example.target: ¿Qué bomba escoge usted?
example.native: Which pump do you choose?

verbs.note: Spelling change g to j in the yo form only (escojo). Use escoge (usted) with a customer.

example.target: Le muestro la garantía por escrito.
example.native: I'll show you the warranty in writing.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (muestro, muestras), except nosotros. Le is the formal usted indirect object.

lessons.title: Tow Driver Drop-Off and a Disputed Scratch
lessons.objective: Record the tow drop-off with the driver, read back the VIN, mileage and time, and document existing damage with photos.
lessons.explanation:
Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (llegó a las 9:40, marcaba 128,450 millas, el VIN termina en 4K7)
La grúa llegó a las 5:40 y la camioneta marcaba 128,450 millas. — The tow truck arrived at 5:40 and the SUV read 128,450 miles.
Tomé 12 fotos y anoté el rayón en la hoja de recepción. — I took 12 photos and noted the scratch on the check-in form.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the technician at check-in, and the AI is tow operator Rigoberto Cano, then owner Daniela Ortiz by phone: record the drop-off, read back the time, VIN and mileage in the preterite (llegó a las…, marcaba…), and document the bumper scratch with photos.

items.note: For a woman: la operadora de grúa.
Say it as one word, "vin"; read the characters back one by one.
Mexican usage: defensa is the everyday word for bumper.

items.target: ¿A qué hora la cargaste en la grúa?
items.native: What time did you load it onto the tow truck?
items.note: Informal, to the tow driver; la refers to la camioneta.
Informal.

items.target: Te leo el VIN: termina en 4K7, ¿correcto?
items.native: Let me read you the VIN: it ends in 4K7, correct?

items.target: El odómetro marca 128,450 millas; anótalo, por favor.
items.native: The odometer reads 128,450 miles; write it down, please.

items.target: Antes de que te vayas, necesito tu firma aquí.
items.native: Before you leave, I need your signature here.

items.target: Señora Ortiz, ya tomé fotos de la defensa trasera.
items.native: Ms. Ortiz, I already took photos of the rear bumper.
items.note: Formal, to the owner on the phone.

items.target: ¿Usted tiene fotos de la camioneta de esta mañana?
items.native: Do you have photos of the SUV from this morning?
items.note: Formal.

items.target: Vamos a revisar todas las fotos, sin culpar a nadie.
items.native: We're going to review all the photos, without blaming anyone.

passage.target: A las 5:40, la grúa de Rigoberto Cano llegó al Taller Ramírez con la camioneta de Daniela Ortiz en la plataforma.
passage.native: At 5:40, Rigoberto Cano's tow truck arrived at Taller Ramírez with Daniela Ortiz's SUV on the flatbed.

passage.target: El operador de grúa tenía prisa, pero el técnico Luis Medina le pidió unos minutos para llenar la hoja de recepción.
passage.native: The tow operator was in a hurry, but technician Luis Medina asked him for a few minutes to fill out the check-in form.

passage.target: Luis: ¿A qué hora la cargaste en la grúa?
passage.native: Luis: What time did you load it onto the tow truck?

passage.target: Rigoberto: La cargué a las 5:05 en la casa de la clienta, y aflojé las correas de amarre hace un minuto.
passage.native: Rigoberto: I loaded it at 5:05 at the customer's house, and I loosened the tie-down straps a minute ago.

passage.target: Luis: Llegaste aquí a las 5:40, ¿verdad?
passage.native: Luis: You got here at 5:40, right?

passage.target: Rigoberto confirmó la hora, y Luis la escribió en la hoja como la hora de entrega.
passage.native: Rigoberto confirmed the time, and Luis wrote it on the form as the drop-off time.

passage.target: Luis: Te leo el VIN: termina en 4K7, ¿correcto?
passage.native: Luis: Let me read you the VIN: it ends in 4K7, correct?

passage.target: Rigoberto revisó sus papeles, comparó el número y también la placa, y dijo que todo coincidía.
passage.native: Rigoberto checked his papers, compared the number and also the license plate, and said that everything matched.

passage.target: Luis giró la llave para ver el tablero y le dijo a Rigoberto: El odómetro marca 128,450 millas; anótalo, por favor.
passage.native: Luis turned the key to see the dashboard and said to Rigoberto: The odometer reads 128,450 miles; write it down, please.

passage.target: Después, Luis caminó alrededor de la camioneta y encontró un rayón de 6 pulgadas en la defensa trasera.
passage.native: Then Luis walked around the SUV and found a 6-inch scratch on the rear bumper.

passage.target: También vio una pequeña abolladura en la puerta del conductor, y Rigoberto dijo que ya estaba allí cuando cargó la camioneta.
passage.native: He also saw a small dent on the driver's door, and Rigoberto said it was already there when he loaded the SUV.

passage.target: Luis tomó 12 fotos con fecha y marcó la abolladura como daño previo en la hoja de recepción.
passage.native: Luis took 12 time-stamped photos and marked the dent as pre-existing damage on the check-in form.

passage.target: Luis: Antes de que te vayas, necesito tu firma aquí.
passage.native: Luis: Before you leave, I need your signature here.

passage.target: Rigoberto puso su firma junto al rayón anotado y se fue con la grúa a las 5:58.
passage.native: Rigoberto put his signature next to the noted scratch and left with the tow truck at 5:58.

passage.target: Minutos después, Daniela Ortiz llamó por teléfono y dijo que el rayón no estaba allí esta mañana.
passage.native: A few minutes later, Daniela Ortiz called on the phone and said the scratch was not there this morning.

passage.target: Luis: Señora Ortiz, ya tomé fotos de la defensa trasera.
passage.native: Luis: Ms. Ortiz, I already took photos of the rear bumper.

passage.target: Luis: ¿Usted tiene fotos de la camioneta de esta mañana?
passage.native: Luis: Do you have photos of the SUV from this morning?

passage.target: Daniela respondió que sí, y Luis le dijo con calma: Vamos a revisar todas las fotos, sin culpar a nadie.
passage.native: Daniela answered yes, and Luis told her calmly: We're going to review all the photos, without blaming anyone.

example.target: La grúa llega al taller con la camioneta.
example.native: The tow truck arrives at the shop with the SUV.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. In the preterite, yo is spelled llegué (g becomes gu before e).

example.target: Rigoberto carga la camioneta en la plataforma.
example.native: Rigoberto loads the SUV onto the flatbed.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. In the preterite, yo is spelled cargué (g becomes gu before e).

example.target: Luis toma 12 fotos con fecha de la defensa trasera.
example.native: Luis takes 12 time-stamped photos of the rear bumper.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Preterite: tomé, tomaste, tomó.

example.target: Anótalo en la hoja de recepción, por favor.
example.native: Write it down on the check-in form, please.

verbs.note: Anótalo is an informal tú command with an attached pronoun, so it takes a written accent.

example.target: Revisamos todas las fotos con la clienta.
example.native: We review all the photos with the customer.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Preterite: revisé, revisaste, revisó.

lessons.title: Saying No: Customer Wants the Airbag Light Cleared
lessons.objective: Refuse to clear an airbag warning light without a repair, explain the risk and the legal issue, and offer a real diagnosis.
lessons.explanation:
Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no lo maneje así; no recomiendo que lo venda sin repararlo)
No lo maneje así; la bolsa de aire podría no funcionar. — Don't drive it like this; the airbag might not work.
No recomiendo que lo venda sin repararlo. — I don't recommend that you sell it without repairing it.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the technician, and the AI is Patricia Navarro, who wants her airbag light turned off before selling her car: refuse politely, explain the safety and legal risk with negative commands (no lo maneje así) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, and offer a real diagnosis.

items.note: Supplemental restraint system; techs say it letter by letter: ese-erre-ese.
Many US shops just say el clockspring.
For a woman: la compradora.

items.target: Lo siento, señora Navarro, no puedo borrar esa luz sin repararla.
items.native: I'm sorry, Ms. Navarro, I can't clear that light without repairing it.
items.note: Formal.

items.target: Si la apago, el problema sigue ahí.
items.native: If I turn it off, the problem is still there.

items.target: Con esa luz encendida, la bolsa de aire podría no abrirse.
items.native: With that light on, the airbag might not deploy.

items.target: No desconecte la batería para apagar la luz.
items.native: Don't disconnect the battery to turn off the light.
items.note: Formal negative command: no + usted subjunctive form.

items.target: No recomiendo que el comprador lo maneje así.
items.native: I don't recommend that the buyer drive it like this.

items.target: Ocultar una falla de seguridad al comprador le puede traer problemas legales.
items.native: Hiding a safety fault from the buyer can bring you legal problems.

items.target: Lo que sí puedo hacer es un diagnóstico hoy mismo.
items.native: What I can do is a diagnosis today.

items.target: No se preocupe, primero vemos qué código tiene guardado.
items.native: Don't worry, first we'll see what code it has stored.
items.note: Formal.

passage.target: Patricia Navarro llega el jueves con su Toyota Camry 2012 a un taller de una plaza comercial en San Antonio.
passage.native: Patricia Navarro arrives on Thursday with her 2012 Toyota Camry at a repair shop in a strip mall in San Antonio.

passage.target: Patricia: Vendo el carro el sábado y necesito que apague la luz de advertencia antes de que llegue el comprador.
passage.native: Patricia: I'm selling the car on Saturday and I need you to turn off the warning light before the buyer arrives.

passage.target: El técnico, Daniel Reyes, le explica que esa luz significa que el sistema SRS detectó un problema.
passage.native: The technician, Daniel Reyes, explains to her that the light means the SRS system detected a problem.

passage.target: Daniel: Lo siento, señora Navarro, no puedo borrar esa luz sin repararla.
passage.native: Daniel: I'm sorry, Ms. Navarro, I can't clear that light without repairing it.

passage.target: Daniel: Con esa luz encendida, la bolsa de aire podría no abrirse.
passage.native: Daniel: With that light on, the airbag might not deploy.

passage.target: Patricia insiste: Mi primo dice que basta con desconectar la batería un rato.
passage.native: Patricia insists: My cousin says it's enough to disconnect the battery for a while.

passage.target: Daniel: No desconecte la batería para apagar la luz.
passage.native: Daniel: Don't disconnect the battery to turn off the light.

passage.target: Patricia: Pero el carro anda bien, y la venta ya está acordada con un señor de Austin.
passage.native: Patricia: But the car runs fine, and the sale is already agreed with a man from Austin.

passage.target: Daniel: No recomiendo que el comprador lo maneje así.
passage.native: Daniel: I don't recommend that the buyer drive it like this.

passage.target: Daniel le aclara que la responsabilidad legal podría caer sobre ella si hay un accidente y la bolsa no se abre.
passage.native: Daniel makes it clear that the legal liability could fall on her if there is an accident and the airbag doesn't deploy.

passage.target: Daniel: No recomiendo que lo venda sin repararlo, y no le pida a otro taller que borre la luz.
passage.native: Daniel: I don't recommend that you sell it without repairing it, and don't ask another shop to clear the light.

passage.target: Daniel: Lo que sí puedo hacer es un diagnóstico hoy mismo.
passage.native: Daniel: What I can do is a diagnosis today.

passage.target: Daniel: No se preocupe, primero vemos qué código tiene guardado.
passage.native: Daniel: Don't worry, first we'll see what code it has stored.

passage.target: Con el escáner, Daniel lee el código guardado en el módulo SRS, y el código apunta a una falla del resorte de reloj.
passage.native: With the scanner, Daniel reads the stored code in the airbag control module, and the code points to a fault in the clock spring.

passage.target: Antes de tocar nada, Daniel desconecta la batería y espera el tiempo que indica el fabricante; después revisa el conector amarillo debajo del asiento y el sensor de ocupante, y los dos están en buen estado.
passage.native: Before touching anything, Daniel disconnects the battery and waits the time the manufacturer specifies; then he checks the yellow connector under the seat and the occupant sensor, and both are in good condition.

passage.target: Según el procedimiento del fabricante, también revisa con el escáner los datos del sensor de impacto delantero y del pretensor del cinturón, y ambos funcionan bien.
passage.native: Following the manufacturer's procedure, he also checks the front crash sensor and seat belt pretensioner data with the scanner, and both work fine.

passage.target: Daniel le da un presupuesto por escrito, y la reparación quedará en el historial de reparación para que el comprador lo vea.
passage.native: Daniel gives her a written estimate, and the repair will go into the repair history so the buyer can see it.

passage.target: Patricia acepta: Está bien, prefiero vender un carro seguro.
passage.native: Patricia agrees: All right, I'd rather sell a safe car.

example.target: Si la apago, el problema sigue ahí.
example.native: If I turn it off, the problem is still there.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In the usted command and the subjunctive, g becomes gu: apague.

example.target: No borro la luz sin una reparación.
example.native: I don't clear the light without a repair.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Shops say borrar el código or borrar la luz for clearing a fault code.

example.target: No recomiendo que lo venda sin repararlo.
example.native: I don't recommend that you sell it without repairing it.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (recomiendo, recomiendas), except nosotros. No recomiendo que is followed by the subjunctive.

example.target: No lo maneje así.
example.native: Don't drive it like this.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Manejar is the usual word for driving in Mexico and the US. No lo maneje is the formal usted command.

example.target: Daniel revisa el conector debajo del asiento.
example.native: Daniel checks the connector under the seat.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb.

lessons.title: Feedback After a Drain Plug Comeback
lessons.objective: Give a tech clear, respectful feedback on a leaking drain plug and agree on the steps for the next oil service.
lessons.explanation:
Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (quiero que cambies la arandela siempre; te recomiendo que uses el torque que indica el fabricante)
Quiero que cambies la arandela del tapón en cada servicio de aceite. — I want you to replace the drain plug washer at every oil service.
Te recomiendo que uses el torque que indica el fabricante. — I recommend that you use the torque the manufacturer specifies.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You are the lead tech, and the AI is tech Julio Castañeda: give him clear, respectful feedback on the drain plug comeback and agree on steps for the next oil service, using quiero que and te recomiendo que with the present subjunctive.

items.note: Many Mexican techs say la rondana.
Many US shops also just say el comeback.
In Mexico, the parking area at a house, covered or not.
Use el cliente for a man.
Ponerse a la defensiva = to get defensive.

items.target: Julio, ¿tienes un minuto para hablar del regreso de ayer?
items.native: Julio, do you have a minute to talk about yesterday's comeback?
items.note: Informal: tú between coworkers.

items.target: La clienta regresó con una mancha de aceite en su cochera.
items.native: The customer came back with an oil stain on her driveway.

items.target: No te estoy culpando; quiero que lo resolvamos juntos.
items.native: I'm not blaming you; I want us to solve it together.
items.note: Quiero que + subjunctive: resolvamos.

items.target: Te pido que cambies la arandela aunque se vea bien.
items.native: I'm asking you to replace the washer even if it looks fine.
items.note: Te pido que + subjunctive: cambies.

items.target: Es importante que hagas la revisión de fugas antes de bajarlo.
items.native: It's important that you do the leak check before lowering it.

items.target: Entiendo que te moleste, pero esto nos afecta a todos.
items.native: I understand it bothers you, but this affects all of us.

items.target: ¿Qué necesitas de mí para que no vuelva a pasar?
items.native: What do you need from me so it doesn't happen again?
items.note: Para que always takes the subjunctive.

items.target: Señora, disculpe la molestia; ya le cambiamos la arandela.
items.native: Ma'am, sorry for the trouble; we've already replaced the washer.
items.note: Formal: usted with the customer.

passage.target: En la sala de descanso de la agencia, Andrea Ruiz, la técnica líder, se sienta con el técnico Julio Castañeda antes del turno.
passage.native: In the dealership's break room, Andrea Ruiz, the lead tech, sits down with tech Julio Castañeda before the shift.

passage.target: Andrea: Julio, ¿tienes un minuto para hablar del regreso de ayer?
passage.native: Andrea: Julio, do you have a minute to talk about yesterday's comeback?

passage.target: Andrea: La clienta regresó con una mancha de aceite en su cochera.
passage.native: Andrea: The customer came back with an oil stain on her driveway.

passage.target: Andrea: Al revisar el carro, vimos que la arandela del tapón era la vieja y que el cárter goteaba aceite por el tapón.
passage.native: Andrea: When we checked the car, we saw that the drain plug crush washer was the old one and that the oil pan was dripping oil at the plug.

passage.target: Julio se pone a la defensiva y dice: Esa arandela se veía bien, y yo llevo 10 años haciendo cambios de aceite.
passage.native: Julio gets defensive and says: That washer looked fine, and I've been doing oil changes for 10 years.

passage.target: Andrea: No te estoy culpando; quiero que lo resolvamos juntos.
passage.native: Andrea: I'm not blaming you; I want us to solve it together.

passage.target: Andrea: Entiendo que te moleste, pero esto nos afecta a todos.
passage.native: Andrea: I understand it bothers you, but this affects all of us.

passage.target: Andrea: Cada regreso nos cuesta tiempo y también la confianza de la clienta.
passage.native: Andrea: Every comeback costs us time and also the customer's trust.

passage.target: Andrea: Te pido que cambies la arandela aunque se vea bien.
passage.native: Andrea: I'm asking you to replace the washer even if it looks fine.

passage.target: Andrea: También te recomiendo que uses el torque especificado que indica el manual del fabricante y que no lo calcules a ojo.
passage.native: Andrea: I also recommend that you use the specified torque that the manufacturer's manual indicates and that you don't eyeball it.

passage.target: Andrea: Es importante que hagas la revisión de fugas antes de bajarlo.
passage.native: Andrea: It's important that you do the leak check before lowering it.

passage.target: Julio respira y admite: Tienes razón, fue un error, pero ya tenía la costumbre de reusar la arandela.
passage.native: Julio takes a breath and admits: You're right, it was a mistake, but I already had the habit of reusing the washer.

passage.target: Andrea: ¿Qué necesitas de mí para que no vuelva a pasar?
passage.native: Andrea: What do you need from me so it doesn't happen again?

passage.target: Julio: Quiero que pongamos arandelas nuevas junto a la charola de drenaje y que agreguemos ese paso a la lista de verificación.
passage.native: Julio: I want us to put new washers next to the drain pan and to add that step to the checklist.

passage.target: Andrea: Gracias por aceptar la retroalimentación; hoy mismo agrego el paso a la lista y dejo una caja de arandelas nuevas en tu área.
passage.native: Andrea: Thanks for accepting the feedback; today I'm adding the step to the checklist and leaving a box of new washers in your area.

passage.target: Acuerdan que en el próximo servicio de aceite Julio firme la lista después de la revisión de fugas y que Andrea revise el primer carro con él.
passage.native: They agree that at the next oil service Julio will sign the checklist after the leak check and that Andrea will check the first car with him.

passage.target: Después, Julio llama a la clienta y le dice: Señora, disculpe la molestia; ya le cambiamos la arandela.
passage.native: Afterward, Julio calls the customer and tells her: Ma'am, sorry for the trouble; we've already replaced the washer.

example.target: Quiero que cambies la arandela en cada servicio de aceite.
example.native: I want you to replace the washer at every oil service.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (quiero, quieres), except nosotros. When you want someone else to act, use quiero que + present subjunctive.
